questions.stem: What is the main goal of 'assessment for learning'"

options.text: To identify students who can be categorised as 'slow learners'
To evaluate student performance and assign grades
To provide feedback to students that can be used to improve their learning
To compare student performance to a standard or benchmark

questions.expected_answer: To provide feedback to students that can be used to improve their learning
questions.explanation: Assessment for learning, also known as formative assessment, is designed to support and enhance student learning. It involves ongoing, real-time assessments that provide feedback to both students and teachers about their progress and understanding. The primary aim is to help students identify their strengths and weaknesses, understand their areas of improvement, and make necessary adjustments in their learning strategies. This process empowers students to take an active role in their own learning, fostering continuous improvement and growth. It differs from 'assessment of learning' (summative assessment) whose primary purpose is to evaluate and assign grades. Hence,’providing feedback to students that can be used to improve their learning’ is the main goal of ‘assessment for learning’.
questions.supporting_excerpt: What is the main goal of 'assessment for learning'" — Answer: (C) To provide feedback to students that can be used to improve their learning
